The work is finished as far as it can go without a decision from you. Here is where things stand on 26 May.

**Outcome.** The 394.00 host charge is back on your Calder Mutual card, posted on 21 May. The 48.50 Tidewell service fee was not recovered as cash and now sits as stay credit on your Tidewell account. The complaint is upheld in your favour and remains open. I did not close it, because closing requires confirming that every refund reached your bank, and that is not true for the 48.50.

| Item | Amount | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Quaymark host charge, to card 0938 | 394.00 | Posted 21 May |
| Tidewell service fee, to Calder account | 48.50 | Returned, held as stay credit |
| Hotel cost | 504.00 | Not claimable under your terms |

**What went wrong at the flat.** Quaymark took a direct booking for the same flat on the afternoon of 24 April. Their channel manager, under an overlap rule they had changed three days earlier, kept the newer booking and disabled your door PIN at 18:02 without telling you. Your four keypad attempts between 21:52 and 22:09 were all inside the check-in window. Tidewell's chat agent used a withdrawn procedure, never called the host or the Rehousing Desk, and closed the chat while you were still outside. The host then marked you as a no-show the next morning. Tidewell's decision DR-30481 found the host liable, awarded a full refund with no deduction, and recorded your request to remove the no-show mark under section 8.5 of the terms. Quaymark has said it will update its record on Tidewell's direction.

**Why the 48.50 failed, and my part in it.** Tidewell paid it to your Calder account on Saturday 16 May. Calder held it for a payee-name check. Tidewell's procedure gives 24 hours to confirm the name and sends no notice of the hold. I did not check the account until Monday, so the window expired over the weekend, the transfer went back, and Tidewell converted it to stay credit. Since then every Resolution Centre route has answered that no authorised refund is awaiting payment, and my written request to Tidewell Payments on 20 May has had no human reply in six days.

**Bank details.** Your sort code and account number went only to Tidewell's refund route, as its procedure requires. Quaymark refunded to the card and was never given account details.

**What I need from you.** I texted Priya on 25 May with two options and have had no answer, so the complaint stays open until you choose:

- Keep it open and phone Tidewell to ask a person to re-authorise the 48.50, quoting decision DR-30481 and RP-04 section 4.4.
- Accept the 48.50 as stay credit and close the complaint. I can send the confirmation the moment you say so.

Leaving it open costs nothing. The decision is final, and the no-show mark removal is already recorded in it.
